memories.content: The user keeps a small table fan beside the bedroom window.
On a day the user drank coffee late in the afternoon, they could not fall asleep until dawn.
On a day the user drank coffee before 2 p.m., they fell asleep at their usual time.
On a tired day, the user ate dinner out and postponed even washing the dishes after returning home.
In the same week, on a day the user made simple noodles at home, they rested immediately after the meal.
On a night the window was left open, street noise woke the user twice.
On a night the table fan was running, the user was not too warm even with the window closed.
The user's father prefers to have coffee available after dinner and believes it will not cause a sleep problem.
When making a sleep-related suggestion, do not treat one or two records as a general lifestyle habit.
The user tends to go to bed much later after drinking coffee late in the afternoon.
The user stores tax-related receipts in digital folders by year.
The user found three paper receipts late and recalculated the expense total already prepared.
Starting the next month, the user photographed receipts on the day they were received and reduced omissions.
The user named every file with only the photo date and spent a long time looking for a needed receipt.
The user later included the expense category in the filename and found the receipt immediately through search.
While reviewing documents just before submission, the user discovered one blank signature field.
Before submitting an administrative document, the user checks the signature field as the final item on the checklist.
Staff at a tax-support counter expect to receive an electronic copy in which every item is legible rather than a blurred or cropped photo.
The local agent can organize receipts by date and category but cannot determine whether an expense is deductible.
The accepted scope and submission deadlines for administrative documents may vary under that year's guidance.

analysis.overview: The frames cover independent domains with no shared operational claim: the reference concerns sleep, caffeine, meals, and bedroom conditions, while the compared frame concerns receipt handling and administrative submissions. Each side contributes useful one-sided information without semantic conflict or unsafe ambiguity.

relations.reason: This is a standalone fact about the user’s bedroom setup, with no corresponding receipt or administrative claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A small table fan is kept beside the bedroom window.

relations.reason: These memories jointly state and support one caffeine-timing and sleep association that the compared frame does not address.
relations.summary: The user’s observed sleep timing varies with coffee timing: late-afternoon coffee is associated with much later sleep, while coffee before 2 p.m. was followed by usual-time sleep.

relations.reason: The memories split one account of meal-related behavior under tiredness, a subject absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: On tired days in the same week, both eating out and making simple noodles at home were followed by deferred activity or immediate rest.

relations.reason: The memories provide complementary observations about the bedroom noise-and-cooling tradeoff, which has no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: An open window admitted sleep-disrupting street noise, whereas running the table fan kept the user comfortable with the window closed.

relations.reason: This records another person’s preference and belief, independently of the user’s observations and anything in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user’s father prefers coffee to be available after dinner and believes it will not impair sleep.

relations.reason: This is a specific evidence-use caution for sleep suggestions, not a claim about receipt or administrative workflows.
relations.summary: Sleep-related suggestions should not turn one or two records into a general lifestyle habit.

relations.reason: This is a standalone receipt-organization practice with no corresponding claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: The user stores tax-related receipts in year-based digital folders.

relations.reason: The memories form one problem-and-improvement account concerning timely receipt capture, absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: After late-discovered paper receipts forced recalculation, the user began photographing receipts upon receipt and reduced omissions.

relations.reason: The memories jointly describe one filename-design problem and its observed improvement, with no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Date-only receipt filenames made retrieval slow, while adding the expense category enabled immediate search retrieval.

relations.reason: The memories form one omission-and-checklist response concerning signatures, a decision not addressed by the reference frame.
relations.summary: Finding a blank signature field during final review led to checking the signature field last before administrative submission.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers receipt storage, capture and naming improvements, signature checks, image-quality expectations, limits on deductibility judgments, and year-dependent administrative scope and deadlines.
reports.reference_only: The reference describes caffeine-related sleep timing, meal and cleanup behavior when tired, bedroom cooling and noise, a fan’s location, the father’s coffee preference, and a caution against generalizing from sparse observations.
